To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The moduli space approximation is a useful tool for studying the scattering of massless and/or massive magnetic monopoles; (2) The scattering of massless monopole clouds off massive monopoles is described by a process that involves the interaction of a thin shell with the massive core; and (3) The interaction is strongest for shells that overlap the massive core at a time when they are small in size.

the time evolution of a class of non-Ablian soliton solutions in a spontaneously broken gauge theory.
the time evolution of the moduli space of monopoles.
the dynamics of magnetic monopoles in a non-Abelian gauge theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction between the massless and massive particles is weak.
the interaction between massless monopole clouds and massive cores can be described as a scattering of a thin shell.
the scattering of massless monopole-antimonopole pairs in an SU(N+1) theory is not a good description of what happens in a theory with a spontaneously broken SU(N) symmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scattering of massless and/or massive monopoles is a process which is very sensitive to the details of the initial configurations.
, in a theory with a large number of massless monopole constituents, the interaction between them is very weak and the scattering of the cloud is essentially elastic.
, although the cloud is a very complicated field configuration, its interaction with the massive monopole cores is quite simple and well described by the scattering of point particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in the absence of a mass gap, the scattering of massless and heavy objects can be studied using the moduli space method.
the interaction between a cloud of massless particles and a massive object is not a simple one.
the moduli space description is not only valid for the time evolution of the massless monopole cloud, but it also captures the scattering of this cloud off massive objects.
